items.title: Puma Shen, Critic of China, Could be the Next Mayor of Taipei
items.excerpt: Puma Shen, who has been sanctioned by China for his efforts to prepare civilians for an invasion, could become Taiwan’s next political star if he wins.

items.title: Plaque by Plaque, Russia Erases the Memory of the Gulag’s Horrors
items.excerpt: The Kremlin’s rehabilitation of Stalin, who presided over the brutal labor camps of the Gulag, has accelerated during Russia’s war in Ukraine.

items.title: Spain’s Far-Right Era Ended in 1975. Will This Man Change That?
items.excerpt: If the polls are right, Santiago Abascal’s Vox party could become the first far-right group to join a Spanish government since the days of Franco.

items.title: Johannesburg Lawmakers Snub Helen Zille in Mayoral Election
items.excerpt: The selection of Herman Mashaba to lead South Africa’s wealthiest city was a blow to Helen Zille, the candidate whose party won the most votes in the election.

items.title: A Journalist Fights for Free Speech in Egypt, and to Stay Out of Jail
items.excerpt: The fate of Lina Attalah and her news outlet, Mada Masr, in two court cases is seen as a test of whether the country’s independent press can survive.

items.title: Russia’s Big Ambitions for A.I. Are Undercut by Constraints of War
items.excerpt: Russian officials see artificial intelligence as a way to solve the country’s pressing problems. But Russia’s technological development has been held back.

items.title: Quebec Can Keep Its Ban on Religious Symbols, Canada’s Top Court Rules
items.excerpt: In a landmark decision, the Supreme Court backed the province’s use of a constitutional override while leaving the door open to future legal scrutiny.

items.title: France’s Bookstores, Beloved Curators of Literature, Are in a Deep Crisis
items.excerpt: Caught between rising costs and price regulations, French booksellers are closing at a record pace, depriving new authors of vital shelf space.

items.title: The Threat to a Sanctuary for Children of North Korean Defectors
items.excerpt: A school in Seoul caters to students whose parents fled North Korea. Neighbors want it gone, and students say it is just one example of the prejudice they face in the South.

items.title: Japanese Volleyball Player Rui Takahashi Makes Waves By Coming Out as Gay
items.excerpt: Rui Takahashi, 26, has made waves as one of only a few professional athletes to come out as gay in Japan.

items.title: Lured by High Salaries, Some Brazilians Were Duped Into Fighting for Russia
items.excerpt: Dozens of Brazilians were sent to the front lines with little training, and the high salaries they were promised, they say, turned out to be illusory.

items.title: After Cyberattacks and Bomb Threats Hit Europe, Survivalism Goes Mainstream
items.excerpt: More governments in Europe are telling citizens to prepare for emergencies. After unexpected disruptions, many are listening.

items.title: Net Migration to U.K. Falls to Lowest Level Since 1997, Excluding Pandemic
items.excerpt: The drop was largely driven by fewer people arriving from outside the European Union. It reflects government action to restrict immigration after a public backlash.

items.title: U.K. Releases Files on Peter Mandelson, Ambassador Tied to Jeffrey Epstein
items.excerpt: Documents released Thursday shed new light on the rushed appointment of Peter Mandelson and his continued ties to Global Counsel, a lobbying group.

items.title: Police Link Release of Substance at Don Toliver Concert to Robbery Attempts
items.excerpt: The police in Manchester, England, said they believed “organized criminals targeted people in the crowd to commit a series of robberies” during the concert on Sunday night.

items.title: Princess Kate’s Cancer Documentary ‘Heal’: 3 Takeaways
items.excerpt: ‘Heal,’ a 30-minute authorized documentary released this week, offers glimpses into Catherine’s recovery since her 2024 cancer diagnosis and treatment.

items.title: Spanish Police Find a Vast Marijuana Bunker Beneath a Backyard Playground
items.excerpt: Five people were arrested in southern Spain after a large marijuana farm was found under a playhouse on artificial turf.

items.title: Climate Talks Imploded, but the ‘Age of Electricity’ Rolls On, Energy Chief Says
items.excerpt: Fatih Birol, head of the International Energy Agency, said that market forces, data centers and energy security are driving the clean transition anyway.

items.title: Why Russia Is Erasing Stalin’s Crimes
items.excerpt: Across Russia, memorials to victims of Joseph Stalin’s repressive regime are being quietly dismantled as more and more critics of the war in Ukraine are jailed. Our Moscow correspondent Valerie Hopkins takes us to one example of this erasure.

items.title: Ontario Premier Says He’d Use a Gun to Protect His Family
items.excerpt: Recent home invasions have stirred unease in Toronto. On Thursday, the premier of Ontario said he would fire a gun in self-defense ‘in a heartbeat.’

items.title: In Praise of My Typewriter
items.excerpt: The A.I. projects editor at The New York Times uses chatbots every day. But when it’s time to write, he reaches for an Olivetti Lettera 22 from the 1950s.

items.title: Two Italians Killed in Iranian Drone Attack on Kuwait, Officials Say
items.excerpt: The deaths follow a series of strikes on Gulf Arab states that host U.S. military facilities in recent weeks as talks to end the war continue to stall.

items.title: Gérard Depardieu Is Ordered to Stand Trial Over Rape Accusation
items.excerpt: The actress Charlotte Arnould has accused the French movie star of raping her in 2018. He has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

items.title: El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele Elates Haiti With Fight Against Gangs
items.excerpt: The president of El Salvador has widespread support among Haitians, who are tired of violence and hope he can be the one to finally end it.

items.title: The E.R. Closed at 5 P.M. A Dying Woman Showed Up 11 Minutes Too Late.
items.excerpt: In rural British Columbia, Courtney McCowan died after paramedics tried to help her in a hospital’s parking lot.

items.title: How Birds With GPS and Audio Sensors Track Hidden Fishing Boats
items.excerpt: Researchers are using seabirds equipped with GPS and audio gear to detect vessels that operate with no tracking signals and to assess the environmental hazards they pose.

items.title: Brazilian Duped Into Fighting for Russia: ‘War Is Hell’
items.excerpt: Dozens of Brazilians have joined the Russian army, some say lured by a pair of recruiters promising money and adventure. Here is one soldier’s story.

items.title: Attack Blamed on ISIS Kills 2 Syrian Security Force Members
items.excerpt: The assault on a security headquarters in the northeastern city of Hasakah was carried out by four militants who local officials linked to the Islamic State.

items.title: Hong Kong Grieves Fire Victims Under Watchful Eye of Authorities
items.excerpt: The city’s residents quietly mourned the 168 lives lost in a high-rise complex blaze a year ago, as officials warned against using the disaster to sow division.

items.title: London Banning Noise and Capping Fares for Its Pedicabs
items.excerpt: Starting Friday, the city will regulate pedicab operators for the first time, imposing fare caps and noise restrictions.
